page: Vultr voc-s-4c-32gb-640s-amd is an instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute series built on the x86_64 architecture. The platform provisions 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by 2 physical AMD EPYC cores operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz with simultaneous multithreading. Cache resources consist of 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB shared L3 cache. Supported instruction sets include AES, SHA-NI, and AVX, while AVX-512 extensions are absent. Memory capacity is sized at 32 GB, establishing an 8:1 gigabyte-to-vCPU ratio. Storage is bundled as a 640 GB local NVMe SSD, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address, with no GPU acceleration hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread execution alongside typical four-thread parallel limits. In stress-ng single-core testing, the instance scores 3,199.17, placing in the top 10 percent, while Geekbench single-core reaches 2,128.0 and text processing reaches 2,837.0. Multi-core performance aligns with the middle 50 percent, scoring 12,814.11 in stress-ng and 6,709.0 in Geekbench. PassMark database operations and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 25 percent quartile. In memory tests, uncached read bandwidth reaches 86.9 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 60.95 GB/sec, supporting Redis throughput of 8.74 million SET operations per second. LLM inference remains modest due to the lack of specialized matrix hardware.

The instance offers a high memory-to-CPU ratio and substantial local NVMe storage, which provides qualitative cost efficiency for operations that require high memory capacity without the expense of paying for larger virtual CPU counts. The primary tradeoff lies in limited multi-threaded throughput and lack of vector acceleration beyond standard AVX. These characteristics align the server with in-memory caching tiers, text parsing pipelines, staging environments, and memory-bound backend applications.

With an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the system emphasizes memory density over high parallel core density. Benchmarks demonstrate top-tier single-threaded performance and text processing, balanced by average multi-core metrics and uncached memory bandwidth of 86.9 GB/sec. Redis SET throughput measures 8.74 million operations per second, while multi-threaded decompression and database operations reflect the constraints of a four-thread ceiling. This server provides balanced resource efficiency for memory-intensive applications, in-memory caches, and text-processing workflows that benefit from local NVMe storage.
